title: Squat Everyday vs Widow makers squats for hypertrophy
summary: NH compares squatting every day (high frequency, medium-high intensity, low volume) with widowmaker squats (one 20+ rep set, low frequency, moderate intensity). Squatting daily builds squat strength and technique, but widowmakers produce more tonnage and muscle damage and are strictly better for leg hypertrophy. Pick widowmakers for size, squat-every-day for strength.

claims.claim: He has never run either squat-every-day or widowmaker squats long enough to give personal data.
Very frequent or very high-volume squatting is conducive to progress because it accumulates huge tonnage and, as a big compound interfering with all lower-body lifts, makes recovery easy to assess.
Both methods produce results, but widowmaker squats are strictly better for hypertrophy.
Squatting every day makes you very proficient: technique and neurological adaptation improve and the squat goes up fast.
Squat-every-day must run at medium-to-high intensity varied through the week, not maximal daily; with frequency maxed, volume has to sit between low and medium.
Bulgarian-style daily max squatting sits even further toward the high-intensity extreme than squat-every-day.
Widowmaker squats are done once a week or once every 4 days, for a set of 20+ reps at moderate intensity; you can't use 85% for that rep count.
Volume is a jealous mistress: high volume trumps your ability to also train with high intensity and high frequency, even when frequency is low.
The driving force of hypertrophy is tonnage, not just volume; volume without intensity is often lacking.

Squat-every-day warm-ups tend to be singles to spare recovery, so little tonnage accumulates; widowmakers need fewer warm-up steps but lifters still ramp with more reps to be fully warm for the all-out set.
A 20-rep set at 235 lb yields several times the tonnage of a heavy single at 350 lb; even 3-4 days of daily heavy squats (300, 280-290, 275) still total less than one widowmaker session.
Widowmakers tear up muscle fibers and cause the worst DOMS while leaving long recovery; squatting daily taxes the nervous system and strength output but causes less fiber damage.
After a widowmaker you need about 72 hours just to squat light again, and roughly 20 more hours for optimal recovery.
Combining frequency and intensity correlates strongly with strength gains, whereas volume is king for size.

Widowmakers force high-intensity reps because the squat lets you rest-pause at lockout and recover enough for 1-2 more reps; only the overhead press compares, while resting at deadlift lockout doesn't help.
Bulgarian-style squatting gives even better strength but even less hypertrophy because intensity control is non-existent; the Wisconsin method is not great for hypertrophy either.
Choose widowmakers for leg size and squat-every-day for strength, though neither is required to build bigger legs.
Unless you have very long femurs and are very tall, bigger quads are probably the most attainable goal for natural lifters.

exercises.name: Squat every day
cues: vary intensity through the week, not maximal daily
exercises.why: technique and neurological adaptation, fast strength gains on the squat

exercises.name: Widowmaker squat
cues: one set of 20+ reps at moderate weight
rest at the top with the bar to grind extra reps
ramp warm-ups so legs are fully ready
exercises.why: most tonnage and muscle damage, best for quad hypertrophy
